note: E620 grammar profiles of the F2 plain-text script family, read by plaintext.cjs (field reference in its header). Regular expressions are JavaScript source strings. Order matters: the first profile whose match passes owns a folder.

profiles.source: Suika 2 (MIT) src/script.c, tool/package.c and its successor OpenNovel (MIT) src/file.c + docs/md_en/reference.md: txt/*.txt scripts; data01.arc = u64 count, {char name[256], u64 size, u64 offset (absolute)}; since 2.x names and bodies XORed with a stream from the build key (default cafef00dabadbeef; other keys: add them to table.cipher.suika). *name*[voice*]text, @choose / @ichoose label text …, \n, \^{ruby}, \#{color} … inline, a leading \ continues the message
NVList user guide ch20 (Apache-2.0): text lines, @ Lua line, @@ Lua block, # comment, ## comment block; [ ] inline Lua; @choice("a", "b") options
VNDS .scr format (digital-haze script_format.txt via the BASLQC/vnds wiki): text <string> (@ no wait, ~ / ! blank), choice a|b|c, everything else a command
CPyMO cpymo_interpreter.c (AGPL, format facts only): script/<name>.txt, #say [name,]text, #text text,x1,y1,…, #title text, #sel n then n option lines, #select_text n,opt…

PyWright (github saluk/PyWright, no licence: format facts only) games/<game>/<case>/*.txt: "quoted" lines are text with {n} newlines and {…} markup, nt <name> sets the name tag, list / li <option> / showlist choices, # comments, lowercase commands

INSTEAD (MIT, instead-hub): game folder or .zip with main3.lua (stead3) / main.lua, header -- $Name: …$; every string literal ("…" or '…') holding non-ASCII text is a line; ^ is a line break; [[ ]] long strings across lines and .idf containers are not read

AIRNovel (MPL-2.0): config.anprj (XML, first_script) + mat/*.an scripts, KAG-like [tag a=b], ; comment, *label, &expr&; speaker / choice / ruby tags not documented; a build packed into package.nw is taken by the TyranoScript fingerprint first
Kaleido ADV Workshop: M2 PSB archive pairs scenario_info.psb.m + scenario_body.bin (Squirrel 2 scripts), encrypted with a 13-character key kept in the exe: recognised only, the key needs a real game
